solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drunk in street, boss right to enter The Three Bells?

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the next letter goes into the other words
a drunk staggers about, so these letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone drunk in the street while the boss is going into a pub called The Three Bells.
explanation.walkthrough: The Three Bells looks like a pub sign, but Charlotte, Emily and Anne Bronte first published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: The three novelist sisters took the pen surname Bell, so the trio were literally the three Bells.

clue.text: Undisciplined brat, heiress in Trollope's county

indicators.note: something undisciplined is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spoilt child and a rich heiress misbehaving somewhere in the setting of a Victorian novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope set his Chronicles of Barsetshire in this imaginary English county.

clue.text: Level at condo partially raised, using smaller base?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read from bottom to top
partially means only part of the run of words is used

parts.note: the end of Level, all of at and the start of condo

explanation.surface: A builder checking the floor level at a condo, raised up on a smaller base.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the letters straddling Level, at and condo upwards. The smaller base is smaller than the usual base ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Octal numbers count in base eight, a smaller base than ordinary decimal arithmetic.

clue.text: Lob rugby player giving reminder of an earlier time

parts.note: to lob is to throw
backs are the players behind the scrum in rugby

explanation.surface: A rugby player lobbing the ball reminds an onlooker of the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: A throwback is something that recalls, or reverts to, a type from the past.

clue.text: One of the first cities captured by wild Masai warrior

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor
wild letters run free and settle in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
Ur in Mesopotamia was one of the earliest cities

explanation.surface: An ancient city seized by fierce Masai warriors from East Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The Masai fit the warrior picture, but the word is only letters; the warrior is Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of the military caste of feudal Japan.

clue.text: Women laid up — could this get them going?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: Anne stands for any woman, so women are Annes

explanation.surface: Women laid up in bed, constipated, waiting for something to get them moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Laid up suggests illness, which feeds the laxative picture, while also signalling the upward reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna is a plant-based laxative, taken to get the bowels moving again.

clue.text: Eliot's editor associating pen with last letter in period

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the word for a span of time

parts.note: an era is a period of history
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
a pound is a pen for animals

explanation.surface: T S Eliot's editor, at work with a pen, adding the final letter to a full stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Pen and period sound like writing kit, but pen is an animal enclosure and period a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet heavily edited Eliot's The Waste Land, cutting it to its published form.

clue.text: Habitual boozer very troublesome to start with

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired

indicators.note: to start with points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of troublesome; the letters running backwards across 'to start' are a coincidence

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker who is a real nuisance from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: A sot is a person who is habitually drunk.

clue.text: Warrant ingenuity needed to defend rook

indicators.note: defenders surround what they protect, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: wit is quick ingenuity
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A chess player needing cleverness to protect a rook under attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written order from a court, such as a warrant.

clue.text: Soldiers guarding one in Paris deserve pay

indicators.note: guards stand around what they protect, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps
un is French for one
to rate something is to deserve it, as in it rates a mention

explanation.surface: Troops guarding someone in Paris feel they have earned their wages.
explanation.definitionFit: To remunerate is to pay someone for work done or services given.

clue.text: Stop blooming predator returning to access its prey?

indicators.note: to access is to get inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: deer are a wolf's typical prey

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a wolf is a predator

explanation.surface: A hunting animal doubling back to reach its quarry, and a plant that won't stop flowering.
explanation.walkthrough: Stop blooming is a verb phrase: to stop something blooming by stripping its flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflower literally means to strip a plant of its flowers, ending its bloom.

clue.text: Animal in mountain pasture a feline lacking tail

indicators.note: lacking tail means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: an alp is high summer grazing in the Swiss mountains
taken as written
a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: A tailless cat wandering in a high mountain meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American domesticated animal related to the llama.

clue.text: Possibly where criminals meet, but for one?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split as con plus junction: a meeting point for convicts
second meaning: but is an example of a joining word in grammar

explanation.walkthrough: But for one reads like an exception, but it means the word but is one instance. A con is a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, a word such as and or but that links clauses belongs to this part of speech.

clue.text: With which to announce eg Hungary's first goal?

definitions.text: With which to announce eg Hungary's first
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the breathy sound used to pronounce the opening letter of Hungary
second meaning: an ambition or hope

explanation.walkthrough: Hungary's first goal suggests football; it is the letter H, sounded with a breath, and then a separate meaning, goal.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics the breathed h sound has this name, and the word also means an ambition.

clue.text: Peninsula where cool friend holds party

indicators.note: something that holds another has it inside

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
china is a friend, from Cockney rhyming slang china plate for mate
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A trendy friend throwing a party somewhere on a peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: The party goes between the first two pieces, so cool friend together does the holding.
explanation.definitionFit: Indochina is the Southeast Asian peninsula containing Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia and neighbours.

clue.text: Woman without issue one stopping useless soldier

indicators.note: a stopping plugs a gap, so this piece sits inside the others

parts.note: null means void, of no use
a para is a paratrooper
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A childless woman, the one obstacle blocking a hopeless soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Nullipara is the medical term for a woman who has never given birth.

clue.text: Army presence perhaps in Dublin Bay occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Troops occasionally seen around Dublin Bay.
explanation.walkthrough: Army reads as military, but here it is arm plus y: something present in an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two forearm bones, so it is found in an arm.

clue.text: Pet dog losing ball, coming across new discovery

indicators.note: coming across means spanning another piece, so it goes around it
losing a ball means dropping the round letter

parts.note: Fido is the stock name for a pet dog
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A pet dog that has lost its ball stumbles on something new.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog's name loses its last letter, the ball shape, then wraps around the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A find is something discovered, especially a valuable one.

clue.text: Item for making rolls in the kitchen, or boiler house

parts.note: a kettle is the boiler kept in a kitchen
drum is British slang for a house or home

explanation.surface: Kitchen equipment for making bread rolls, or the house's boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolls in the kitchen suggests baking, but the rolls are drum rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettledrum, or timpani, is the orchestral instrument for drum rolls.

clue.text: Monster movie?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: huge, enormous, used as an adjective
second meaning: James Cameron's 1997 film about the sinking liner

explanation.walkthrough: Monster movie suggests a horror film; split it into an adjective meaning huge and a famous film.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means colossal, and it is also the title of the blockbuster film.

clue.text: I'm quite sure arts graduate's about to eat in!

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts
acid etches by eating into metal

explanation.surface: A confident arts graduate, sure they are about to dine in.
explanation.definitionFit: Betcha is a casual spelling of bet you, said when certain of something.

clue.text: Potato dish fine, or a pudding served up cold?

parts.note: aloo is potato in Indian cookery, as in aloo gobi
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an alternative route to the same letters: a fool is a fruit pudding, and fool with a, turned upwards, gives the same word

explanation.surface: Choosing between a potato dish and a cold pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: A second route also works: a fool is a fruit pudding, and fool plus a, served up, reads the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof is distant and unfriendly, which is a cold manner.

clue.text: Tour extremely tiny church, finding artwork

parts.note: a trip is a tour

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of tiny
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Touring a very small church and discovering a painting there.
explanation.definitionFit: A triptych is a three-panelled painting, often an altarpiece in a church.

clue.text: In Yorkshire, the plant that might choke river?

parts.note: Yorkshire dialect shortens the to t'
weeds choke garden plants

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire weed that might clog a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is the river forming part of the border between England and Scotland.

clue.text: State in case that's set in corrupt Carolina

indicators.note: set in means placed inside the other piece
corrupt means spoilt or twisted, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the place name taken as letters
if means in case, as in take a coat if it rains

explanation.surface: A legal case in a crooked Carolina court, moved to another state.
explanation.walkthrough: Carolina looks like the state wanted, but it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: California is a US state on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Suitable for the occasion, having a pint

parts.note: taken as written
PT is the abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: Having a pint seems just right for the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means appropriate or fitting in the circumstances.

clue.text: Lake in Ireland viewed from the east

indicators.note: in an across entry, viewing from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A lake in Ireland as seen from its eastern shore.
explanation.walkthrough: In Ireland suggests the lake is Irish; it is one of North America's Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Erie is one of the five Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Character on Baywatch warned off after dealing?

indicators.note: after means this piece comes behind the next one in the answer

parts.note: to traffic is to deal, usually illicitly

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of place, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Baywatch lifeguard character warned off after some shady dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Baywatch is the beach TV show, but here it means watching parking bays; a traffic warden is the British official who tickets parked cars.
explanation.definitionFit: This parking official patrols parking bays, so watching bays is literally the job.
